calc.faq_intro: Parcels, pallets, containers, air or sea freight: here are the most common questions about shipping goods between Belgium and the DRC.
calc.q_how_send: How do I send a parcel from Belgium to the DRC?
calc.a_how_send:
Start by estimating the cost with the calculator above: enter the weight, dimensions or volume, then compare express, cargo and sea freight for a Brussels → Kinshasa shipment.

Next, prepare sturdy packaging and a clear description of the contents, useful for DRC customs. We collect your parcel at the depot or by pickup, then ship it by air or sea depending on the option chosen, with tracking all the way to Kinshasa.

To prepare everything without missing a step, read our guide:
calc.l_how_send: Sending a parcel from Belgium to the Congo (DRC)
calc.q_price_calc: How is the price of a shipment to Kinshasa calculated?
calc.a_price_calc:
The price of a Belgium → DRC parcel depends on the transport mode and on the higher of the actual weight and the volumetric weight. The calculator at the top of the page instantly shows all three rates — express, cargo and sea — with a line-by-line breakdown.

Every shipment adds a €5 handling fee. Under-customs shipments may carry a €125 administrative fee. Beyond the online limits (very large volume, another destination…), the estimate automatically switches to a quote request.
calc.q_weight: Does the price depend on weight or volume?
calc.a_weight:
Both. For each shipment we compare the actual weight (what the scale reads) and the volumetric weight (the bulk). The higher of the two is the basis for billing, for air freight as well as cargo.

Volumetric weight is calculated with the formula L × W × H (cm) ÷ 6000. When the volume exceeds the actual weight, the difference is billed at €8/kg. A light but bulky parcel, such as a box of clothes, is therefore billed on its bulk.
calc.a_volumetric:
Volumetric weight reflects the space a parcel takes up, regardless of its actual weight. It is calculated by multiplying length × width × height in centimetres, then dividing by 6000.

A bulky but light parcel takes up room on the aircraft or in the container: this calculation prices that space. If the volumetric weight exceeds the actual weight, the difference is billed at €8/kg on top of the actual weight.
calc.q_volume_calc: How do I calculate a parcel's volume in cubic metres?
calc.a_volume_calc:
To get the volume in cubic metres (m³), multiply length, width and height expressed in metres. In centimetres, calculate L × W × H then divide by 1,000,000: a 60 × 40 × 40 cm box is thus 0.096 m³.

Volume is used to price sea freight (per m³) and to determine volumetric weight for air freight. For a full step-by-step, read our guide:
calc.q_air_vs_sea: What is the difference between shipping by air and by sea?
calc.a_air_vs_sea:
Air freight is fast: ideal for urgent shipments, small and medium parcels and valuable goods, it is measured in days. Sea freight is far more economical by volume — perfect for large shipments, pallets and containers — but it is measured in weeks.

In short, air prioritises speed and sea prioritises price for large volumes. To choose based on your goods, read our guide:
calc.l_air_vs_sea: Air or sea freight: which to choose
calc.q_when_air: When should I choose air freight?
calc.a_when_air:
Choose air freight when time matters most: urgent shipments, documents, samples, small and medium parcels, high-value goods. Express covers 0.1 to 200 kg (€18/kg, €18 minimum) and cargo up to 500 kg (€16/kg).

Beyond these limits, or for a very large volume, sea freight is generally more suitable and more economical.
calc.q_when_sea: When should I choose sea freight?
calc.a_when_sea:
Sea freight is the right choice for large volumes, house moves, pallets and container shipments, when timing is not critical. It is billed per cubic metre: €750/m³, and €725/m³ from 5 m³.

It is the most economical way to move large quantities of goods between Belgium and the DRC, arriving via the port of Matadi and then on to Kinshasa.
calc.q_multi: Can I send several parcels or small parcels together?
calc.a_multi:
Yes. The calculator has a "number of identical parcels" field to estimate a grouped shipment, and the €5 handling fee is charged only once per shipment, not per parcel.

Grouping several small parcels into one shipment (consolidation) often lowers the cost per kilo or per m³. For parcels of different sizes, ask us for a quote and we'll optimise the whole shipment.
calc.a_bulky:
Yes. Bulky goods usually travel by sea freight, billed per m³, which stays economical even for large volumes. Enter the dimensions or volume in the calculator for a first estimate.

calc.q_pallet: Can I send a pallet to the DRC, and how does it work?
calc.a_pallet:
Yes, we ship pallets from Belgium to the DRC, most often by sea freight. For an estimate, enter the pallet's dimensions or volume (in m³) in the calculator: the sea rate applies per cubic metre.

Depending on size and volume, we arrange the shipment as consolidation (you only pay for the space used) or as a dedicated load. For one or more pallets of palletised goods, it's best to:
calc.q_container: Can I ship in a container (consolidation or full container)?
calc.a_container:
Yes. For large volumes, shipping by sea container is the most economical option. With consolidation you only pay for the space your goods take up in the container, without renting a whole container; depending on the volume we also offer a dedicated container.

The container travels by ship to the port of Matadi, then we arrange road transport to Kinshasa. To understand consolidation and how it works, discover:
calc.q_customs: What are the customs fees and under-customs fees?
calc.a_customs:
They are two separate things. The "under-customs fees" on Luna's side are a €125 administrative fee that applies only to under-customs shipments; they are then added to the €5 handling fee. A standard shipment pays none.

Import duties and taxes in the DRC are set by Congolese customs according to the nature and value of the goods; they are paid on arrival and are not included in the transport price. To understand who pays what (transport, customs, VAT) depending on the Incoterm, read our guide:
calc.l_customs: Incoterms, DAP vs DDP and shipping costs
calc.q_delay: What are the transit times for air or sea shipments?
calc.a_delay:
As a rule, air freight is measured in days and sea freight in weeks, but the exact time depends on the chosen mode, the period and customs formalities. Sea freight transits via the port of Matadi before the final leg to Kinshasa.

We confirm the precise transit time for your shipment at booking or with your quote, so you get reliable information rather than a rough estimate.
calc.a_deliver_kin: Yes. Kinshasa is our main destination: our online rates cover the Brussels → Kinshasa route by express, cargo and sea freight. The estimate from the calculator matches this route.

Our online rates cover Brussels → Kinshasa. For another DRC city (Lubumbashi, Matadi, Goma…) or another origin, shipping is still possible but the rate is set case by case.

api_docs.meta_description: Pedagogical guide to using the Luna Tracking API: first request in 3 minutes, authentication, endpoints, cURL examples, error handling.
api_docs.hero_intro: Everything you need to plug your tools into Luna Tracking — explained plainly, with concrete examples.
api_docs.what_p1: An API is a door Luna Tracking opens to your tools (website, Excel script, ERP, mobile app…). Instead of retyping your shipments by hand, your tool asks Luna a question in HTTP and gets the answer back as JSON.
api_docs.what_p2: Nothing to install on our servers, no VPN, no gateway — just URLs like any website, except they return data instead of pages.
api_docs.what_analogy_body: The client (your tool) is you at the table. The waiter (the API) takes your order, checks you're allowed to order, and fetches the dish from the kitchen (the database). You never see the kitchen — and that's a good thing.
api_docs.today_intro: The API is already live. These use cases work out of the box:
api_docs.today_c1_b: Fetch the shipment list for a business — reference, status, route — perfect for an internal dashboard.
api_docs.today_c2_b: Full detail by ID: packages, tracking, dates, consignee.
api_docs.today_c3_b: Your B2B address book, exportable in one request.
api_docs.today_c4_b: Currency + weight + volume → available modes and customer prices, no account required.
api_docs.quick_intro: Goal: receive a real response from the API in under 3 minutes. Open a terminal (or an online one like reqbin.com).
api_docs.quick_s1_title: Check the API is up (no account needed)

api_docs.quick_s1_expect: Expected response (the time field will differ):
api_docs.quick_s1_check_body: If you got that JSON, the API is reachable from your machine. Otherwise: check your connection and re-copy the command carefully.
api_docs.quick_s2_body: Endpoints that touch YOUR data need a key. Here's how:
api_docs.quick_s2_l1: Sign up on Luna Tracking and pick "Professional" during onboarding.
api_docs.quick_s2_l4: Click "New key", give it a name, tick the permissions, generate.
api_docs.quick_s2_warn_title: Heads up: the key is shown ONCE
api_docs.quick_s2_warn_body: On generation, copy the full key immediately and store it in a password manager. If you lose it: revoke it and create a new one. We cannot show it to you again.
api_docs.quick_s3_body: Replace YOUR_BUSINESS_ID with your business ID (visible on the dashboard) and lk_live_xxx.YOUR_SECRET with your actual key.
api_docs.auth_title: 4. How you prove who you are
api_docs.auth_intro: The API accepts two ways to authenticate: one for your app (Bearer JWT), one for scripts and integrations (ApiKey). Each request carries the token in the Authorization header; the API verifies it, then answers or refuses.
api_docs.auth_bearer_body: Generated when a human signs in. Great for web/mobile apps where a user drives the request. Expires in one hour and auto-refreshes client-side.
api_docs.auth_apikey_body: A long-lived key, tied to YOUR business only. Never expires but can be revoked at any moment. The right choice for a cron, an ERP, a webhook, a nightly export.
api_docs.auth_never_title: Never in the browser, never in Git
api_docs.auth_never_body: An ApiKey grants access to YOUR business data. Never put it in browser JavaScript, don't commit it to GitHub, don't email it. Use a secret manager (1Password, Vault, env variables).
api_docs.resp_intro: Every response has the same shape: either { data } (with optional { meta }), or { error } with a code and a message. Write your code once, reuse everywhere.
api_docs.resp_header_body: Each response carries an X-Api-Version header. Check it client-side to be sure you're talking to the right version:

api_docs.ep_usage: Aggregated usage: totals + timeline + top endpoints + per-key breakdown, over the requested window.
api_docs.ep_perms_body: When you create a key, you pick what it can do. A minimal tick list keeps the blast radius small if the key leaks.
api_docs.oa_intro: The API is described in OpenAPI 3.1 — the standard machine-readable format. Import it directly into Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, Swagger Editor, or any SDK generator. The file is served live from our server: every new API version reflects automatically.

api_docs.err_intro: Errors always look like { error: { code, message } }. Code the field, not the message (which may be translated).
api_docs.err_missing_param: A required parameter is missing (e.g. business_id).
api_docs.err_bad_id: An ID is not a valid UUID.
api_docs.err_unauth: No token, or an expired / invalid token.

api_docs.limits_intro: The API is currently free. Every call is logged (method, path, status, response time) so we can one day propose fair plans — but no paywall today.
api_docs.limits_free_body: No strict rate limit for now. If you plan thousands of requests per hour, tell us first — we prefer being warned rather than seeing you blocked. A paid tier (Free / Pro / Business / Enterprise) will be announced if volume warrants it — existing customers will get at least 30 days' notice.
api_docs.roadmap_intro: The next chantiers, in order. We won't paywall the API until these bricks are ready.
api_docs.roadmap_i1: Write endpoints (POST /shipments, POST /quotes) — create and update from your tools.
api_docs.roadmap_i2: Webhooks — receive an automatic ping when a status changes (shipment.in_transit, quote.accepted…).
api_docs.roadmap_i3: OpenAPI/Swagger documentation — auto-generate SDKs in your favourite language.
api_docs.roadmap_i4: Official SDKs (JS/Python) — no more cURL to type.

That is where our job starts: a trusted partner collects them on site, we consolidate them with other shipments to bring the transport cost down, then we ship them to their final destination. You follow every step from your Luna account.

legal_terms.page_intro: These general terms govern all transport, logistics, handling and ancillary services performed by Luna Tracking Logistics SRL. The principal accepts them without reservation by the mere handing over of the goods.
legal_terms.s1_body:
These General Terms (hereinafter "GT") govern all transport, logistics, handling and ancillary operations carried out by LUNA TRACKING LOGISTICS (hereinafter "the Carrier") on behalf of any customer (hereinafter "the Principal").

These GT apply to every contract of carriage evidenced by a transport document (air waybill, sea waybill, CMR consignment note or delivery note), unless expressly agreed otherwise in writing.

The Principal accepts these GT without reservation by the mere handing over of the goods to the Carrier.
legal_terms.s2_body:
**2.1 Packaging**

The Principal is solely responsible for packaging. Goods must be packed so as to withstand the normal stresses of transport (handling, stacking, temperature and pressure variations). The Carrier cannot be held liable for damage resulting from defective packaging, even if apparent.

**2.2 Declarations and documentation**

The Principal must provide all required declarations and documents (customs, sanitary, certificates of origin). Any error, omission or delay in documentation is the sole responsibility of the Principal.

**2.3 Dangerous and prohibited goods**

Handing over dangerous goods (per IATA/IMDG/ADR classifications) without prior written declaration and the Carrier's agreement is strictly prohibited. Any discovery of undeclared dangerous or prohibited goods (explosives, toxic substances, counterfeits, cash, etc.) will result in:

- immediate refusal or destruction of the goods at the customer's expense;
- invoicing of crisis-management and clean-up costs;
- reporting to the judicial and customs authorities.
legal_terms.s3_body:
**3.1 Best-efforts undertaking**

The Carrier undertakes to use all reasonable means to move the goods but does not guarantee the time of arrival nor connection with any specific event (unless a guaranteed transit time is agreed in writing).

**3.2 Temperature-controlled goods (cold chain)**

For temperature-controlled goods, the Principal must provide self-contained insulated packaging (cool boxes, ice packs) able to maintain the required temperature for a period exceeding the theoretical transit time by 24 hours. The Carrier does not provide an active cold chain (unless under a specific contract) and declines all liability for a break caused by the customer's packaging.
legal_terms.s4_body:
The Carrier's liability is limited in accordance with the applicable international conventions and national laws, except in case of gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

**4.1 Air transport (Montreal Convention)**

In case of destruction, loss, damage or delay, compensation is limited to 22 SDR (Special Drawing Rights) per kilogram of gross weight of the goods lost or damaged (article 22 of the Montreal Convention). Note: the SDR value fluctuates. As an indication, 1 SDR ≈ €1.20 (to be checked on the day of the loss).

**4.2 Sea transport (Hague-Visby Rules)**

Liability is limited to 2 SDR per kilogram of gross weight or 666.67 SDR per package or unit, whichever is higher, unless a higher value has been declared.

**4.3 Road transport (CMR Convention, where applicable)**

Compensation is limited to 8.33 SDR per kilogram of gross weight missing or damaged.

**4.4 Exclusions**

The Carrier is not liable for:

- inherent vice of the goods (intrinsic defect, perishability);
- the customer's fault (packaging, loading by the customer);
- force majeure (strikes, weather, government decisions, pandemics);
- indirect damage (loss of business, loss of market, commercial prejudice).
legal_terms.s5_body: The liability limits above often leave a significant shortfall compared with the real value of the goods. The Principal is expressly advised to take out "ad valorem" or all-risks transport insurance with its own insurer. The Carrier takes out no insurance on the customer's behalf unless instructed in writing and the corresponding premium is paid.
legal_terms.s6_body:
**6.1 Invoicing**

Rates are based on quotes, the air waybill or the applicable rate schedules. The chargeable weight is the higher of the gross weight and the volumetric weight (IATA formula: L × W × H / 6000 or 5000 depending on the service).

**6.2 Payment terms**

Unless otherwise agreed, invoices are payable on receipt or within 30 days of the invoice date.

**6.3 Late payment**

Any late payment automatically entails, without prior notice:

- late-payment interest at the statutory rate in force in Belgium + 8% (or as per the law of 2 August 2002);
- a fixed recovery indemnity of at least €40.

**6.4 Right of retention**

In the absence of payment when due, the Carrier reserves the right to exercise a lien over all goods entrusted to it (even those belonging to third parties or shipped on behalf of other principals) until full payment of the sums due, pursuant to article 21 of the Belgian law of 28 December 1931 or equivalent provisions. The goods may only be sold with judicial authorisation or under the statutory pledge procedures.
legal_terms.s7_body:
**7.1 Receipt**

The consignee must check the condition of the goods on delivery.

- Apparent damage / partial loss: reasoned reservations must be recorded on the transport document on delivery.
- Concealed damage: reservations notified by registered letter within 7 days of receipt (Montreal Convention).
- Delay: claim within 21 days of the goods being made available.

Failing compliance with these time limits, any action against the Carrier is inadmissible (time-barred).
legal_terms.s8_body: These terms are governed by Belgian law. In the event of a dispute, and failing an amicable settlement, the courts of the judicial district of the Carrier's registered office (Brussels) have exclusive jurisdiction, even in case of multiple defendants or third-party proceedings.

legal_privacy.page_intro: Luna Tracking Logistics processes your personal data in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Belgian law of 30 July 2018. This page explains what data we collect, why, and what your rights are.
legal_privacy.s1_body: The data controller is Luna Tracking Logistics, whose details appear above. For any question about your data: info@lunatrackinglogistics.com.
legal_privacy.s2_body:
- **Quote requests and messaging**: name, email, phone, shipment details, the content of your messages.
- **Customer account**: email, password (encrypted), name, shipment and order history.
- **Shop & Ship orders**: products ordered, recipient name, phone and address in the Congo. Payment is handled by our payment provider; we do not store your card details.
- **Parcel tracking**: tracking number and data of the shipment consulted.
- **Technical data**: IP address, browser and pages visited, in our host's logs, for site security.
legal_privacy.s3_body:
- Preparing a quote and performing the transport or order (performance of the contract).
- Replying to your messages and providing customer follow-up (performance of the contract, legitimate interest).
- Meeting our legal, accounting and customs obligations (legal obligation).
- Securing the site and preventing fraud (legitimate interest).

We do not send marketing without your consent and we never sell your data.
legal_privacy.s4_body: Your data is accessible to our team and to our technical processors: Supabase (database and authentication, EU servers), Cloudflare (hosting and security), Resend (email delivery), our payment provider for online orders, as well as the carriers, customs agents and logistics partners strictly necessary to move your shipment, including in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Transfers outside the European Union are governed by the European Commission standard contractual clauses or are necessary for the performance of the transport contract.
legal_privacy.s5_body: Quote data and messages: 3 years after the last contact. Account data: as long as the account is active, then 3 years. Transport and invoicing documents: 7 years (accounting obligation). Technical logs: 12 months at most.
legal_privacy.s6_body: You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, port and object to the processing of your data, and to withdraw your consent at any time. Write to info@lunatrackinglogistics.com; we reply within one month. You may also lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (Rue de la Presse 35, 1000 Brussels — www.dataprotectionauthority.be).
legal_privacy.s7_body: This site uses no advertising cookies and no third-party audience measurement. Only strictly necessary items are stored in your browser: your login session, chosen language, cart contents and the token of your support conversation. They require no consent.
legal_privacy.s8_body: Exchanges with the site are encrypted (HTTPS). Access to data is limited to authorised staff. Passwords are stored encrypted. In the event of a data breach likely to affect you, we will inform you as required by law.
legal_privacy.s9_body: This policy may be updated to reflect changes in our services or in regulation. The date of the last update is shown at the top of the page.

incoterms.sea_only_warning: This Incoterm is for sea freight only; for air or road shipments use FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU or DDP.
incoterms.EXW_desc: The seller makes the goods available at its premises; the buyer handles loading, export clearance, all transport and all risks.
incoterms.FCA_desc: The seller hands the export-cleared goods to the buyer's carrier at the agreed place; risk passes to the buyer at that point.
incoterms.CPT_desc: The seller pays transport to the destination, but risk passes to the buyer as soon as the goods are handed to the first carrier.
incoterms.CIP_desc: Like CPT, and the seller also buys all-risks insurance up to the destination.
incoterms.DAP_desc: The seller delivers to the agreed place, ready for unloading; the buyer pays unloading, import clearance and duties.
incoterms.DPU_desc: The seller delivers and unloads at the agreed place; the buyer handles import clearance and duties.
incoterms.DDP_desc: The seller bears all costs and risks up to the destination, including import clearance, duties and taxes.
incoterms.FAS_desc: Sea only: the seller places the export-cleared goods alongside the vessel at the port of loading; the buyer bears everything after that.
incoterms.FOB_desc: Sea only: the seller loads the goods on board at the port of loading; risk passes on board and the buyer pays the freight.
incoterms.CFR_desc: Sea only: the seller pays freight to the destination port, but risk passes to the buyer once the goods are loaded on board.
incoterms.CIF_desc: Sea only: like CFR, and the seller also buys minimum insurance up to the destination port.
